overall_explanation: Reviewed the Rust source changes against the surrounding code (pair_admission.rs, pair.rs, spawn.rs, native.rs, linux-pidfd-spawn). The dispatch composition is sound: identity is minted only from the matched OwnedChild via retain_identity() after a second liveness check, the Probe test double returns None and AdmittedPeer::serve rejects None with Invalid before any PF20 call, and serve_owned_child re-verifies the SO_PEERPIDFD peer against the retained identity. RootDispatch enforces same-pair identity (Arc::ptr_eq on control), one handler per role, and generation equality; every failure path (open error, worker role, ownership/duplicate/generation mismatch, thread start failure, job return/panic) cancels the pair, and the AdmittedPeer RAII drop inside the job closure guarantees channel fencing independent of polling. Drop joins outstanding jobs, which is bounded because PairChild::stop shuts down the admission guard sockets (shutdown is socket-wide, so the serve clone sees EOF) and serve_channel configures 10s timeouts. Module/feature gating is consistent: `launch` is already behind `synthetic-fixture`, the new `synthetic_fixture` module and re-export are gated on linux/gnu + feature, and the optional tempfile dep follows the existing `dep:codex-linux-pidfd-spawn` target-table pattern; Cargo.lock/MODULE.bazel.lock invariance is plausible since tempfile was already a dev-dep edge. The fixture accepts no caller paths/keys/UIDs and only creates fresh 0o700 temp roots via the crate-private enroll. Scope matches the fifteen allocated paths plus coordinated bookkeeping, and the retained RTX evidence (including the original failing compile/test runs) is consistent with the final six-case pass. No landable-blocking defects found.
